rows.en:
I decided to go with him.
After all, I was the one who'd dragged him into this.
When I told the girls from my class who'd come to me for advice, they said they'd come along too. Maybe they felt responsible as well.
So the same group as before went back to that restroom one more time.{p}

The same spiritual aura as before hung in the restroom.
This time Mr. Wakatsuki seemed to feel it too, and he looked very uneasy.{p}

Mr. Wakatsuki stood in front of the stain and stared at it for a while.
We stood behind him and watched to see what would happen.{p}

"Aaaaaaaaagh!"
After staring at the stain for a while, Mr. Wakatsuki suddenly screamed and staggered backward.
We'd been standing right behind him, so when he backed into us and fell against us, we lost our balance and went down.
He was thrashing around, shouting "Stay away! Stay away!", but I was pinned underneath him, so I couldn't see a thing.
The girl who'd been standing next to me must have been able to see it, because she screamed and burst into tears.
And then, mixed in with her cries, I suddenly heard a woman's voice, low and menacing.
"You, I will never forgive.
You who mocked me, I will never forgive."{p}

...But there was nothing there.
No sign of Mr. Wakatsuki either.{p}

At that moment, the stain suddenly started to bulge out of the wall.
In the end it pulled itself free of the wall and began drifting through the air.
They said they could faintly see long hair around the stain's face, and the faint shape of a sailor uniform where its body was.
The drifting stain moved toward Mr. Wakatsuki.
Then, the instant it seemed to wrap itself around him, he melded into the stain and vanished.
After that, the stain that had swallowed him slipped back into the wall where it had been, and disappeared.{p}

That's what their stories added up to.
{a}, can you believe it? This story?
I couldn't believe it at first either.
But no matter how many days went by, Mr. Wakatsuki never came to school, and it's a fact that the weight of him lying on top of me suddenly vanished.
I had no choice but to believe what they told me.
I heard this later, but apparently the pattern of that stain in the restroom changed a little.{p}

Naturally.
I'm a boy, after all.
But {a}, you're a girl, so you have the chance to check whether there's a new face in the mouth of that stain.
Next time you go to that restroom, go and check it out for me.
I'll be looking forward to it.
But you have to be careful.
You'd better not mock that stain, or look at it just out of curiosity.
If what the girls in my class said is true, it might just pull you in.{p}Well, that's the end of my story.
Who's next, I wonder?{p}

"Th-this is serious, Hosoda.
This is definitely the work of a spirit."
"What, really?★"
I couldn't help asking him again.
"Yes.
This is quite grave.
I felt an incredible spiritual aura the moment I walked into this restroom.
This is the real thing.
It's almost a wonder nothing has happened until now.
I can feel a powerful grudge coming from this stain."
By the time he'd said that much, the girls with us had burst into tears.{p}

"Sir, what should we do?"
At that point, all we could do was rely on him, right?
It didn't seem like a problem I could do anything about.
"Hosoda, I'm going to perform an exorcism.
The preparations will take time, so you'd all better go home now."
That's what he said.
I was worried about him, so I asked if there was anything I could do to help.{p}

But he said he'd always had a strong sixth sense, which was why he'd gotten interested in the occult, and he'd done a lot of research on exorcism too, so he'd be fine.
Even so, I was worried about him, so I decided to wait outside the restroom.{p}

Those of us left behind talked it over in front of the restroom.
"Maybe you girls should go home?
From the way he talked, it sounds pretty dangerous..."
That's what I told the girls who were with me.
The girls said they'd go home first and leave the rest to me, and off they went.{p}

I waited in front of the restroom until he came back.
...After a while, he returned carrying a cardboard box.{p}

It must have held the things he needed for the exorcism.
He warned me firmly that I must never come in, and went into the restroom alone.{p}

I could hear his voice from inside.
I couldn't make out what he was muttering, but now and then I'd hear him raise his voice.
I was dying to know what was going on in there.
What do you even do in an exorcism...?
As time went by, that question turned into curiosity.{p}Desperate to take a peek, I...
Took a peek inside
Didn't peek

I just had to know what was going on inside, so I decided to take a peek.
I figured it'd be all right as long as I watched from a distance.
That was a mistake.
I never dreamed it would turn out like that...
I quietly peeked in from the entrance.{p}

When I stood at the entrance, a wind was blowing from inside.
And the restroom windows weren't even open.
I figured he and the spirit must be clashing.
Drenched in sweat, he was chanting something with all his might.
I turned my eyes to the stain on the wall.{p}

And would you believe it, the air around where the stain was was shimmering, like a mirage rising off the ground.
Now and then, the same expression as the face-shaped stain would surface in that mirage.
I watched the scene with bated breath.
Then, all of a sudden!
I felt something stroke the nape of my neck.
"Aah!"
I couldn't help crying out.{p}

He looked at me and said,
"You idiot!
What are you doing standing there?!"
Mr. Wakatsuki, normally so mild-mannered, yelled at me with an unbelievably fierce look on his face.
That was the moment.
Maybe his concentration had broken, because I felt the spiritual aura suddenly grow stronger.{p}

The aura knocked me back, and I landed on my backside.
It was strong enough to send even me flying, and I was only standing at the entrance.
There was no way he could be all right in there.
Thinking that, I hurried to my feet and looked at him.{p}

"GYAAAAAAAGH!"
To my horror, Mr. Wakatsuki was surrounded by countless things like spirits, and he was shrieking.
All I could do was stand outside the restroom, shaking.
He was gradually losing his life force, as if the aura were sucking out his soul.
His skin dried out and cracked, his eyes sank in, and his whole face became covered in wrinkles.
On top of that, his hair turned white and fell out in clumps...
In the end, he was all withered and crumbling, just like a mummy.{p}

I don't remember anything at all after that.
When I came to, I was asleep on the bed in my own room.
I had no memory at all of how I'd gotten home.
Was it all a dream...?
I prayed that it had been a dream.
...But sadly, it wasn't a dream.
When I went to school the next day, there were several police cars parked there.
Rumor had it that a body had been found in the girls' restroom, dead under strange circumstances.
Apparently Mr. Wakatsuki was found in such a state that no one could identify him.
Like a scrap of cloth in the shape of a person.
{a}.
They say that stain in the restroom is still there.
...And what's more, they say it's gotten bigger than before.
Here's what I think.
This school is home to a lot of spirits.
Maybe, that time, every spirit in the school gathered in that restroom.
Maybe his exorcism called together all the spirits in the school.
And he had the power to stand up to them.
But just because I peeked in out of curiosity...
If I hadn't peeked that time, maybe all the spirits in this school would be gone now...{p}Well, that's the end of my story.
Who's next, I wonder?{p}

Mr. Wakatsuki stared at the stain for a while.
Since he wasn't saying anything, I asked him,
"What do you think, sir?"
Then he stood up, as if he'd suddenly snapped out of it, and answered like this.{p}

"This is nothing.
There's nothing to worry about.
Now, if you've got time to be distracted by silly things like this, hurry home and study or something."
Half angry, we left the restroom.{p}

I mean, wouldn't you be?
He'd gone out of his way to come look at the restroom.
We'd just assumed he was going to do something about it.
The girls went home grumbling and complaining.
I wanted to ask him what he was thinking, so I waited in front of the restroom for him to come out.
After a while, he came out of the restroom.{p}

"What, you haven't gone home yet?"
I asked him,
"Sir, you went all the way to the restroom to look, so what are you playing at?
I was sure you were going to help us with our problem."
...Looking back, that was quite a thing to say.
To a teacher, no less.
But I was really angry at the time.
The words just slipped out.
But he didn't get angry. He answered like this:
"Hosoda.
I've got a nice offer for you. Would you mind coming along with me for a bit?"{p}

I felt like he'd brushed me off, and that made me angry all over again, but I was also curious about this "nice offer" of his.
So I figured I'd at least hear him out, and I followed him.{p}

He took me to the student guidance room.
It was my first time in there, so I couldn't help getting nervous.
He told me not to be so nervous, and made me some tea.
Once I'd calmed down, he began.
"Hosoda, can you guess how old I am?"
He asked out of nowhere.
Without thinking much, I said about thirty.
He really does look about that age.
"Everyone says that.
But actually, I'm fifty-three."
I couldn't laugh at the joke.
I mean, no matter how you looked at him, he couldn't have been much more than thirty.
While I was wondering how to react, he put on a serious face and said,
"It's no wonder you can't believe it.
You see, I've obtained eternal youth."
As he said that, he took his driver's license out of his wallet and showed it to me.{p}

..................
...I couldn't believe it.
I mean, the birth date on the license said Showa 17. That's 1942.
On his driver's license!
I was so stunned, I kept looking back and forth between the license and his face.
He laughed and said,{p}

"Don't look so surprised... Well, I guess that's asking too much.
But you know, Hosoda, even you can obtain eternal youth."
It's simple, he added at the end.
"Are you interested in eternal youth, Hosoda?"
"Sir!
Please tell me the secret of your youth!☆"
I pressed him, practically pouncing on him.{p}

I mean, wouldn't it be great never to grow old?
Don't you think so too, {a}?
That it'd be great to stay young forever?
You're a girl, so you must feel that even more than I do.
I must have had a really intense look on my face then.
He told me not to look so scary, and began telling me the secret of eternal youth.{p}

She was a lively girl who spoke her mind clearly. A very mature girl.
And that girl fell for me.{p}

A teacher and a student. I knew it was wrong, but I started going out with her."
Seeing this unexpected side of him honestly surprised me, but for the moment I just kept quiet and nodded.
"'I'm going to marry you after I graduate,' Kaori always used to say.
At the time, Kaori was still a first-year, so she had almost three years until graduation.
I tried telling her that in three years I'd be thirty-five, a middle-aged man.{p}

And Kaori said this:
She didn't want me getting any older than I already was.
That's impossible, of course.
Kaori was still just a child.
No matter how many times I told her it was impossible, she wouldn't listen.
And then, a while after that, Kaori handed me some suspicious medicine and told me to drink it.{p}

It was a dark, murky, thoroughly suspicious-looking medicine in a tiny vial.
Kaori watched me the whole time I drank it.{p}

I had no choice, so I drank it.
...It was a salty, thick, sludgy liquid.
It tasted like tomato juice with rust in it, mixed with weeds or something.
Kaori made me drink it every day.
She said it wouldn't work unless I drank it every day.
And what do you know?
Day by day my body felt lighter, and the gray hairs that had started showing up on my head disappeared, every last one.
Kaori said it was a magic medicine that could give you eternal youth..."{p}

"So that medicine is the secret of your youth!"
I wanted that medicine so badly I couldn't stand it.
But he said there wasn't any of it left.
And yet, even then, he still looked young.
Even though it was a medicine you had to keep drinking every day.
I thought he was only saying that because he didn't want to share it with me.
"What do you think was in that medicine?"
Mr. Wakatsuki asked me.
I had no idea at all.{p}

Hosoda, would you have the nerve to drink a medicine like that?"
Hearing that story made me feel sick.
I thought, if I'd have to drink something like that, then... but still, I wanted to stay young.
I gave a small nod.{p}

Then he grinned and went on with his story.
"Actually, Kaori died after that.
She collapsed from anemia.
It may have been only a little at a time, but she'd been drawing her own blood every single day.
It would've been stranger if she hadn't collapsed.
She reached her limit and finally collapsed in that restroom... right in front of that stain. She hit her head and died.
I was sad.
No, not because Kaori had died.
Because I couldn't get the medicine that gave me eternal youth anymore.
A week passed after I could no longer drink it.
In that one week, I aged so much I looked like a different person.
It was as if everything I'd held off came back at once..."
Something's not right, I thought.
After all, he was sitting right in front of me, still looking young.
He kept going.
"It was a while after that, I think.{p}

I thought I'd just been dreaming and didn't give it a second thought.
But it wasn't a dream.
From the next day on, I started getting younger again.
And it was around then{p}

I got scared.
Of Mr. Wakatsuki, and of the ghost of that student, Kaori.
I thought I'd better not get any more involved with this teacher.
"Hosoda, a little while ago you said you wanted to know how to stay young forever, didn't you?"
He said it with a smirk.
"That's enough, sir.
That story was a joke, right?
You're just teasing me for fun, aren't you?"
I didn't want to believe his story.
"Then how do you explain this license?
It's not the kind of thing you can forge that easily.
...Well, never mind.
If you ever want eternal youth, remember this.
You offer the girl you love to that stain...{p}

Let it drink the lifeblood of the girl you love.
Don't worry, it'll be fine.
She'll die, but it'll suck every drop of moisture out of her body, until she's so dry and brittle she crumbles at a touch.
After that, just grind her to powder and scatter her over the schoolyard or something, and you're fine.
Losing the girl you love might be sad, but it doesn't matter.
You'll have eternal youth.
There'll be plenty of other girls to take her place.
...Do you know why I'm telling you all this?{p}

Lately, fewer students use that restroom, saying the stain is creepy.
So there's not enough blood anymore to keep me young.
That's why I want you to spread a rumor: 'That stain is just a stain.'
You're the one girls come to for advice.
If it comes from you, Hosoda, the girls will believe it."{p}

Saying "I'm counting on you," he left the guidance room.
With a parting request that I keep all this a secret.
The truth is, besides Mr. Wakatsuki, there are three more teachers at this school who don't age.
Mr. Wakatsuki told me.
{a}, you're in Class 1-E, right?
If I remember right, your homeroom teacher is supposed to be one of them, too...{p}Well, that's the end of my story.
Who's next?{p}

I really wanted to peek inside.
But he'd told me I must never look.
So I gritted my teeth, held back, and waited patiently.
I mean, you see it all the time in manga, right?
A character does something they're not supposed to, and because of that, something terrible happens.
I didn't want any of that.{p}

..................
..................
I wonder how long I waited.
It felt like I'd been waiting for dozens of minutes.
But actually, it was only about ten minutes.
While I was looking out the hallway window, he came out of the restroom.{p}

"Hey, Hosoda.
Sorry to keep you waiting.
It's over. It went fine..."
He must have been exhausted; his face was pale and he was dripping with greasy sweat.
"So everything's okay now?"
I asked brightly.{p}

"Yes, it's okay.
There's nothing to worry about anymore."
Tired as he was, he forced a smile as he answered.
He must have been trying not to worry me.
I asked him to teach me how to do an exorcism sometime, and left.{p}

The next day, when I told the girl who'd come to me for advice, she was overjoyed.
She said now she could go to the restroom without worrying.
So I had them check it for me.
Whether the stain in the restroom was gone.
The girls who'd come to me went together to look at the restroom.
"Hosodaaa!
It's all okaaay!"
The girls reported back to me in cheerful voices.
They said things like they were glad they'd come to me, so I got a bit carried away too.
But I told them it was Mr. Wakatsuki who'd actually done the exorcism, so they should thank him.
The girls agreed.
...That day was fine.{p}

The next day.
Strangely, the girls were all absent from school.
Only the girls who'd come to me for advice.
I thought it was odd, but figured it was a coincidence and let it go.
But even after several days, they didn't come to school.
I asked our homeroom teacher, but the teacher just dodged the question and wouldn't tell me anything.
Before long, a rumor started going around the class that the girls had run away from home or something, and hadn't even been back home.
That was supposedly why the teacher wouldn't tell us anything.
They hadn't gone home since the day after the exorcism.{p}
